investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that was never decided at idx - specifically when the index the call was assigned is later occupied by a different entry - and is the documented Superseded heuristic therefore shadowed by the index-only check?
investigations.hypothesis: drain_notifiers matches on the pending item's assignment in the order `Some((idx, _)) if idx <= decided` first and `Some((idx, ballot)) if ballot < cur_ballot` second, so once the node's decided index covers the assigned index the call resolves Ok(idx) even if leadership moved on and the entry was overwritten; the Ok contract (await its decided log index, and the documented usage 'durably decided at log idx') is then false, and the Superseded heuristic that was written for exactly this leadership-change case never fires.
investigations.discriminator: Construction that isolates the assigned index from its entry: node A is the leader and accepts its own entry at index 1 with its outgoing and incoming traffic cut, so the entry never leaves A; nodes B and C then elect B and decide index 1 with B's own entry; A is let back in and re-syncs, truncating its log to B's and raising its decided index to 1. If A's pending call resolves Ok(1) while the entry at index 1 on A is B's entry and not A's, the index-only check is a false completion; if it resolves Superseded instead, the hypothesis is refuted.

scope.description: Focused construction of one completion-endpoint identity case: an assigned index that is decided while the entry originally assigned to it was overwritten.
assumptions: 3 nodes, majority quorum; in-process delivery under harness control
node 1's traffic is isolated in both directions while node 2 takes over, so node 1's entry cannot be adopted
node 1 is re-admitted through a Promise + AcceptSync cycle, which is the protocol's normal re-synchronization path

experiment.prefix: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) over MemoryStorage, each driven by a real omnipaxos_runtime actor from spawn_actor with a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl. The transport is explicit: a pump task per node moves outgoing messages into a shared queue and a delivery task pops them and calls the receiver's handle_incoming, dropping messages whose sender or receiver is currently isolated (`blocked`/`blocked_in`). Node 1 has leader_priority 10 and becomes the leader after the initial heartbeats. Sequence: node 1 is first isolated in both directions; `node1.append_notify(TestEntry(42))` is then accepted locally at index 1 (its own entry, read back as Undecided) and never leaves the node; `node2.try_become_leader()` makes node 2 the leader with node 3's promise (its log is empty, since node 1's entry never left), and `node2.append_notify(TestEntry(99))` is decided at index 1 by node 2 and node 3; node 1 is then un-isolated and asked to reconnect to node 2, which makes it promise node 2, receive an AcceptSync that truncates its log to node 2's and raises its decided index to 1. investigations.question: Can a full, undrained RuntimeConfig event channel (a subscribed but unread subscribe_events() receiver) stop the single actor task, and with it the node's whole consensus participation - ticks, message handling and every Command reply?
investigations.hypothesis: detect_and_emit_events awaits event_tx.send for every observed transition and is awaited inside the run loop's tick arm, so once the bounded event channel is full the actor task parks inside the tick arm: no further tick() (leader election heartbeat, resend and flush timers), no incoming-message handling, and no Command reply (not even the documented append_notify Timeout, which drain_notifiers would have produced).
investigations.discriminator: Two runs of the same 3-node in-process cluster that differ only in whether an unread event receiver exists: (A) nobody reads events at all (only the receiver the handle itself holds from spawn_actor); (B) a per-node consumer task reads events until a flag is set and then keeps the receiver but stops reading. The hypothesis predicts both variants park the actor after event_capacity transitions; the construction observations contradict that for (B), so the decisive next information is whether the sender in (B) actually observes a full channel - i.e. the real capacity/state of the event channel (Sender::capacity / try_send from a probe) and whether events are still being produced at that moment, rather than a further variant of the freeze symptom.

history.discriminator: An execution that subscribes without draining on every node of a live in-process cluster: if the actor task is parked on the event send, Command round-trips never complete and a fresh append_notify never reaches its 300ms Timeout endpoint, while the same cluster with the same event_capacity but a draining receiver keeps answering commands and decides the same entry.

investigations.question: In the core Sequence Paxos, if a follower's Accepted reply (or the leader's AcceptDecide) is lost, does any timer-driven or self-initiated mechanism restore the leader's knowledge of that acceptance, or does a quorum-accepted entry stay undecided until an unrelated new proposal arrives?
investigations.hypothesis: There is no repair for this direction: resend_messages_leader in Phase::Accept only resends a pending StopSign/its decide and re-Prepares peers that are not promised, and resend_messages_follower in Phase::Accept is an empty arm, so a lost Accepted is never retried by either side; the leader's decision only re-evaluates on a later handle_accepted, i.e. only when some follower accepts something new, which requires an unrelated proposal.
investigations.discriminator: A deterministic in-process simulation (real OmniPaxos instances with a memory storage, manual message delivery and logical ticks): elect a leader, propose one entry, let the follower accept it, drop only that follower's Accepted, then keep ticking and delivering for a fair window with no new proposals, and compare the leader's decided_idx against a control run in which the same message is delivered. If the entry stays undecided in the drop case while both the leader's own acceptance and the follower's accepted_idx show a quorum, the loss is repaired by nothing in that interval; if the entry becomes decided without the message or without a new proposal, the hypothesis is refuted.

scope.description: Bounded probe of whether an event stream the application does not consume (bounded by RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) parks the single actor loop and withholds its command/append_notify endpoints, with a drained-stream control in the same execution.
assumptions: 3 nodes, standard majority quorum, no message loss or reordering beyond the in-process transport, all nodes run in one process on one tokio runtime

event_capacity is set to 64 so the bound is reached inside a bounded window; the source-settled mechanism (send awaits whenever the channel holds event_capacity events) does not depend on the value, only the number of unconsumed transitions does
the handle's event receiver exists from construction, so an application that never subscribes still leaves it unread
excluded: proving the cluster-wide outage (quorum loss) at the 1024 default capacity
schedule independence and any rate bound on how quickly the bound is reached

basis.prefix: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) are built with OmniPaxosConfig::build over omnipaxos_storage::memory_storage::MemoryStorage and driven by three real omnipaxos_runtime actors spawned with spawn_actor, using a harness-local `TestRuntime` (tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; the crate's TokioRuntime behind the tokio_runtime feature is not required). scope.description: Bounded, deterministic probe of whether a lost follower Accepted reply is repaired by the protocol's own resend/retry machinery within a window of 100 resend periods, or only by an unrelated later proposal.
assumptions: 2-node cluster so the write quorum is the leader's own acceptance plus exactly one follower receipt: one dropped message is enough to hide the quorum from the leader
error-free memory storage, FIFO delivery of everything else, no reordering, no crash and no leadership change during the window
one logical step per node equals one tick(), so the 500-step window contains 100 of the configured 5-tick resend periods for both roles

basis.prefix: Deterministic in-process simulation of the core crate: two real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2; configuration_id 1; MemoryStorage; error-free storage) built by OmniPaxosConfig::build, never run concurrently - the harness drives them manually: each step calls tick() on both, drains take_outgoing_messages() into a FIFO, and delivers every message to the receiver's handle_incoming, except that it deliberately discards exactly one PaxosMsg::Accepted (the follower's receipt). Node 1 has leader_priority 1 so the election is deterministic; election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case lost_accepted_leaves_entry_undecided: elect (both nodes Leader/Follower in the accept phase), append one entry at the leader, drop the follower's Accepted, then run 100 resend periods of ticks (500 steps) with everything else delivered; it emits CA_EVENT lost_accepted_window {steps,resend_periods,produced,dropped,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx,follower_accepted_idx,follower_holds_undecided_entry,leader_still_stable} and asserts exactly one Accepted was dropped, the follower really holds the entry as Undecided at index 0 with accepted_idx 1, the leader and the follower are both still at decided index 0, and the leader is still the stable leader. It then appends a second entry on the same state and emits CA_EVENT later_proposal_repairs {steps_until_decided,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx}. Case delivered_accepted_decides is the control: identical, the receipt is delivered, and the entry must be decided inside the same bounded window (CA_EVENT delivered_accepted_decides). The prerequisite the probe relies on is not 'some message was dropped' but the actual per-message operands: which message kinds were produced and which was discarded are printed in the event.

result.summary: Registered the third lead and requested its probe. The question: can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that was never decided at idx, with the documented Superseded heuristic shadowed because drain_notifiers matches the index-based arm first. investigations.question: Can a full, undrained RuntimeConfig event channel (a subscribed but unread subscribe_events() receiver) stop the single actor task, and with it the node's whole consensus participation - ticks, message handling and every Command reply?
investigations.hypothesis: detect_and_emit_events awaits event_tx.send for every observed transition and is awaited inside the run loop's tick arm, so once the bounded event channel is full the actor task parks inside the tick arm: no further tick() (leader election heartbeat, resend and flush timers), no incoming-message handling, and no Command reply (not even the documented append_notify Timeout, which drain_notifiers would have produced).
investigations.discriminator: Two runs of the same 3-node in-process cluster that differ only in whether an unread event receiver exists: (A) nobody reads events at all (only the receiver the handle itself holds from spawn_actor); (B) a per-node consumer task reads events until a flag is set and then keeps the receiver but stops reading. The hypothesis predicts both variants park the actor after event_capacity transitions; the construction observations contradict that for (B), so the decisive next information is whether the sender in (B) actually observes a full channel - i.e. the real capacity/state of the event channel (Sender::capacity / try_send from a probe) and whether events are still being produced at that moment, rather than a further variant of the freeze symptom.

investigations.question: In the core Sequence Paxos, if a follower's Accepted reply (or the leader's AcceptDecide) is lost, does any timer-driven or self-initiated mechanism restore the leader's knowledge of that acceptance, or does a quorum-accepted entry stay undecided until an unrelated new proposal arrives?
investigations.hypothesis: There is no repair for this direction: resend_messages_leader in Phase::Accept only resends a pending StopSign/its decide and re-Prepares peers that are not promised, and resend_messages_follower in Phase::Accept is an empty arm, so a lost Accepted is never retried by either side; the leader's decision only re-evaluates on a later handle_accepted, i.e. only when some follower accepts something new, which requires an unrelated proposal.
investigations.discriminator: A deterministic in-process simulation (real OmniPaxos instances with a memory storage, manual message delivery and logical ticks): elect a leader, propose one entry, let the follower accept it, drop only that follower's Accepted, then keep ticking and delivering for a fair window with no new proposals, and compare the leader's decided_idx against a control run in which the same message is delivered. If the entry stays undecided in the drop case while both the leader's own acceptance and the follower's accepted_idx show a quorum, the loss is repaired by nothing in that interval; if the entry becomes decided without the message or without a new proposal, the hypothesis is refuted.

investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that was never decided at idx - specifically when the index the call was assigned is later occupied by a different entry - and is the documented Superseded heuristic therefore shadowed by the index-only check?
investigations.hypothesis: drain_notifiers matches on the pending item's assignment in the order `Some((idx, _)) if idx <= decided` first and `Some((idx, ballot)) if ballot < cur_ballot` second, so once the node's decided index covers the assigned index the call resolves Ok(idx) even if leadership moved on and the entry was overwritten; the Ok contract (await its decided log index, and the documented usage 'durably decided at log idx') is then false, and the Superseded heuristic that was written for exactly this leadership-change case never fires.
investigations.discriminator: Construction that isolates the assigned index from its entry: node A is the leader and accepts its own entry at index 1 with its outgoing and incoming traffic cut, so the entry never leaves A; nodes B and C then elect B and decide index 1 with B's own entry; A is let back in and re-syncs, truncating its log to B's and raising its decided index to 1. If A's pending call resolves Ok(1) while the entry at index 1 on A is B's entry and not A's, the index-only check is a false completion; if it resolves Superseded instead, the hypothesis is refuted.
